caseResult.hookKind: dev-only hook destroys the real GPUDevice; the device.lost promise drives the engine loss path
caseResult.epochNote: WebGPU has no contextEpoch; deviceState is the public lifecycle observable for this backend.

timing.timingBasis: performance.now() around the real device.lost/onRestored events; frame counts are the primary evidence

caseResult.sizeNote: device.size is 0x0 before and after restore because this page calls init(surface) but never resize() outside the resize case; the swapchain and canvas backing still use the surface CSS metrics. This is not a restore regression.

recoveredFramePng.note: 2D canvas snapshot of the real WebGPU canvas after the first restore and before the terminal second loss, so the recovered frame survives in the artifact.

unobserved.reason: This page loads no network assets for the case and runs no game/runtime loop, so asset refetch and game restart cannot be observed; both stay PENDING rather than claimed true.

secondLoss.note: The terminal failed state ends the run; restore() was called once and refused, not retried.

notes: The directional light is fixed inside the M0 shader; the built public API has no light object.
Texture usage is sample+copy-dst because the WebGPU validator requires copy-dst for supplied bytes.
Build hash is SHA-256 over the engine JS modules the page actually loaded, sorted by path.

The real GPUDevice was destroyed through the dev-only forceWebGpuDeviceLost hook; the device.lost promise drove loss and restore. The second loss is terminal, restore() was called once and refused, and the run ended. Frame counts, not fabricated milliseconds, are the primary evidence.
